'''Muhammad Rafique''' (2 January 1940 — 16 June 1996) was a Pakistani mathematician and professor of mathematics at the Punjab University. He was a versatile scholar who authored [[College textbook|textbooks]] on [[computer language]] and [[special relativity]]. He was the co-author of textbook ''Group Theory for High Energy Physicists'', which was eventually published years after his death in 2016.

==Biographical overview==

Rafique was born in [[Lahore]], [[Punjab, British India|Punjab]] in [[British Indian Empire|British India]] on 2 January 1940 in Lahore, Punjab in India and was educated at the [[University of the Punjab|Punjab University]] where he graduated with [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] with [[first-class honours]] in [[Mathematics]] in 1960.<ref name="OBITUARY by A. Qadir">{{cite web |last1=Qadir, PhD |first1=A. |authorlink1=Asghar Qadir |title=PROFESSOR MUHAMMAD RAFIQUE: AN OBITUARY |url=http://masder.kfnl.gov.sa/bitstream/123456789/3201/2/U05m01v22i02i02ca15.pdf?locale=en |accessdate=28 April 2020}}</ref> He served in the Faculty of Mathematics at the Punjab University where he graduated with [[Master of Arts|MA]] in Mathematics in 1964, and earned a scholarship to study mathematics in the [[United Kingdom]].{{rp|256}}<ref name="Ellis Horwood"/> He attended the [[University of North Wales]] where he graduated with a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Mathematics in 1967.{{rp|256}}<ref name="Ellis Horwood">{{cite book |last1=Saleem |first1=Mohammad |last2=Rafique |first2=Muhammad |title=Special relativity: applications to particle physics and the classical theory of fields |date=1992 |publisher=Ellis Horwood |isbn=978-0-13-827106-0 |pages=257 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qbDvAAAAMAAJ&q=Rafique%201967 |language=en|accessdate=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Upon returning to Pakistan, he joined the Punjab University and taught there until 1971 when he joined the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]] in Italy as a post-doctoral scholar.{{rp|xi}}<ref name="Taylor & Francis, Saleem & Rafique, 2016">{{cite book |last1=Saleem |first1=Mohammad |last2=Rafique |first2=Muhammad |title=Group Theory for High Energy Physicists |date=2016 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=978-1-4665-1064-7 |pages=206 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ojvSBQAAQBAJ&q=Dr.+Muhammad+Saleem+physics |accessdate=27 April 2020 |language=en}}</ref> From 1972 to 1977, Rafique worked at the [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology|Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology]] where he contributed his work on [[fast neutron calculations]] for [[Nuclear weapon|atomic weapons]] which built his interests in the [[theory of relativity]] and [[nuclear physics]].{{rp|74–75}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=ur-Rehman |first1=Shahid- |title=Long road to Chagai |date=1999 |publisher=Shahid-ur-Rehman |location=Islamabad |isbn=9789698500009 |pages=175 |edition=1st |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sNMgAQAAIAAJ |accessdate=28 April 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

From 1977 to 1982, he served on the faculty of [[University of Tripoli]] in Libya, and served as the Head of Department of Mathematics at the Punjab University from 1983 until 1992 when he went to teach mathematics at the [[King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals|King Fahd University]] in [[Saudi Arabia]].<ref name="OBITUARY by A. Qadir"/> His tenure at the King Fahd University was short-lived. He died due to cardiac arrest in June 1996.<ref name="OBITUARY by A. Qadir"/> Although a mathematician, Rafique was a prolific author on physics, was writing a college text on [[group theory]]'s applications on [[high energy physics]] with [[Mohammad Saleem (physicist)|Mohammad Saleem]] at the time of his death in 1992. The college book was eventually published in 2015–2016 by British publisher [[Taylor & Francis]].
